audit_notes: Model: steady diffusion of mobile silicone through the soft layer (xi = depth/L, surface at 0, undepleted layer at 1 with c = mobile concentration) with a Robin condition at the surface representing the platelet-filled skin: D/L dc/dxi(0) = k_skin c(0), k_skin = D*(1-phi)/((1+alpha*phi/2)*L_skin) (Nielsen tortuosity, same matrix diffusivity). Leaching flux J = (D/L) dc/dxi(0). Design: coefficient L*(1-phi)/((1+alpha*phi/2)*L_skin) = 3e-4*0.9/(6*2e-5) = 2.25, c(0) = 20/3.25 = 6.15, J = 3.33e-12*2.25*6.15 = 4.6e-11 kg/(m^2 s). Baseline: conventional oil-containing coating (45 kg/m^3 free oil, 150 um), with the skin reduced to a 5 um unfilled silicone film (phi = 0, i.e. equivalent to no barrier): coefficient 30, J = 2.9e-10 kg/(m^2 s). Expected gain ~84 %, of which most comes from the oil-free, thicker parent layer (-78 %) and the skin adds a factor 0.69. Caveats: Nielsen assumes perfectly aligned, well-dispersed platelets; real sprayed skins reach perhaps half the tortuosity; the in-plane modulus of the skin with 10 vol% aspect-100 flakes rises strongly (Halpin-Tsai: E_skin ~ 10-30 MPa for a 0.3 MPa matrix... order of several MPa), which spreads fouler loads (shear-lag length sqrt(E_s t_s t_b/G_b) = sqrt(1e7*2e-5*3e-4/3.3e4) = 1.3 mm) and raises the release stress; so the barrier and the release function are in conflict. Dimensionless: tortuosity factor 0.15, skin-to-bulk resistance ratio 0.44 (design). Simulation coefficient: skin conductance 7.5e-12 m/s (informational).
